subject: SIG: Incident response & breach notification — runbook sync

Cc: security@greenfintech.com, Peter Salem <peter.salem@greenfintech.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up — incident notification windows and POCs

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the SIG questionnaire so far. Our security team asked a couple of clarifying questions about Redwood's incident response / breach notification process before we complete our intake:

1) Notification windows: you indicate "60–72 hours" in the SIG matrix. Can you confirm whether that is from detection or from confirmation of impact? We need to map to our internal SLA for customer notification.

2) Point people: who are the 24/7 POCs for production-impacting incidents? Please include escalation order (primary, backup, legal, CISO).

3) Exceptions: will Redwood make an SLA exception or extension if ongoing forensic work prevents precise impact quantification within the notification window? If yes, what is the escalation path?

Would you be able to send a short runbook excerpt (contact matrix + notification timeline) we can attach to our intake? A simple spreadsheet or PDF is perfect.

Thanks — trying to close this by EOD Wednesday (10/07).

Best,
Alyssa Chen
Security Manager, GreenFinTech
[GreenFinTech - security intake id: GF-2391]

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@greenfintech.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — incident notification windows and POCs

Alyssa — thanks for the clear questions. Quick responses below; I'm pulling a short excerpt of the runbook and contact matrix and will send it in a separate email (PDF + spreadsheet).

1) Notification window: our standard statement in the SIG is "initial notification within 60–72 hours of confirmed data breach or confirmed material customer impact." Practically that means we trigger the external notification clock once engineering or security has established that customer data or production integrity is materially impacted (i.e., confirmed impact). Detection alone (anomalous alert under investigation) does not start the clock.

2) POCs / escalation order: primary oncall (SRE) -> secondary oncall (Platform) -> on-call security engineer -> security manager -> legal counsel -> CISO. We maintain 24/7 paging for oncall SRE/security. I'll attach the contact matrix with names/titles and backup numbers.

3) Exceptions: we do allow for an extension in tightly scoped forensic cases where notifying would materially jeopardize evidence collection. Extensions require approval from the security manager + GC (legal) and notification to the customer of the delay as soon as it's safe. The runbook excerpt includes the formal escalation to request an exception.

I'll send the runbook excerpt and contact spreadsheet in ~15 minutes. If you want a one-page summary for your intake form, tell me which fields you need and I'll tailor it.

Kimberly Park
Head of Compliance Programs, Redwood Inference
[Attachment to follow: redwood_ir_contact_matrix.xlsx]

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — incident notification windows and POCs

Looping in a legal note so we're aligned for GreenFin's intake:

- We should avoid language that commits to a rigid hours-only SLA. Use "initial notification within 60–72 hours of confirmed material impact, unless restricted by active forensic or law enforcement requirements." That gives us runway.
- For exceptions, require written sign-off from GC (me or delegated counsel) and Security Manager (Vivek). Keep the customer informed with a "we are actively investigating" acknowledgment if we can't share details.
- Also propose adding an option: "customer-facing notification templates" (we already have two: data-exfil and availability-impact) — Kimberly, please include those as links in the runbook PDF.

Laura Bennett
General Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Internal: legal_redlined_runbook.docx referenced]

Hi Alyssa — attaching a short runbook excerpt and the contact matrix for your intake (see attachments). Highlights below to include in your SIG record:

- Initial notification: within 60–72 hours of confirmed material customer impact (detection does not start the clock).
- Escalation order (24/7): Primary oncall (SRE) -> Secondary (Platform) -> On-call Security Engineer -> Security Manager -> Legal -> CISO. Names and backup numbers in the matrix.
- Exception process: exceptions permitted for active forensic/law enforcement reasons; require Security Manager + GC approval; customer acknowledgement provided as soon as safe.
